q-ai-01.Its R-value and the year it was installe: Ask whether the SOP expects you to measure performance, or to know a history you cannot observe in the attic.
q-ai-01.Its chemical composition and fire rating: Could you confirm a chemical makeup or a fire rating with only your eyes and a flashlight?
q-ai-01.Its upgrade cost and the R-value to add: Pricing and upgrade advice sit outside an inspector's scope. Think about describing conditions, not designing improvements.

q-ai-02.A roof leak above that ceiling; refer to: A thermal camera shows temperature, not wetness. Did the stem mention stains, drips, or wet framing anywhere?
q-ai-02.A plumbing leak in the ceiling; call a p: Ask what evidence of water the stem gives you. A cold patch alone shows a temperature difference, not a pipe failure.
q-ai-02.Nothing, because NC excludes measuring R: Not measuring R-values is different from ignoring what you can see. Does that exclusion cover observed conditions too?

q-ai-03.Acceptable, because the attic itself is: Attic vents are sized for slow air exchange. Could they clear a steady stream of warm, wet bathroom air before it condenses?
q-ai-03.Acceptable as long as the duct run is in: Insulating the duct changes the temperature inside it. Does it change anything about where the moisture lands afterward?
q-ai-03.Not reportable; exhaust fans are not in: Check what NC says about bathroom venting systems before deciding exhaust fans sit outside your scope.

q-ai-04.Stop wind-driven rain from entering thro: Baffles sit inside the attic, not at the soffit face. What could a part in that position do about rain outside?
q-ai-04.Hold the insulation tight against the ro: Insulation does its job lying on the attic floor. Ask why anyone would want it pressed up against the roof deck at the eave.
q-ai-04.Block birds and insects from nesting in: Screens on vent openings handle pests. Baffles sit further inside the attic, so think about what they touch there.

q-ai-05.1 sq ft per 50 sq ft, or 1 per 100 with: Those ratios call for far more vent area than real attics carry. The base number sits in the hundreds, not the fifties.
q-ai-05.1 sq ft per 1,500 sq ft, or 1 per 3,000: Picture one square foot of vent serving a 1,500 square foot attic. Would that small an opening move much air at all?
q-ai-05.1 sq ft per 300 sq ft, or 1 per 600 with: A vapor retarder does appear in the venting rule. Recheck whether both numbers here match the IRC base and reduced ratios.

q-ai-06.No; moving insulation is outside the ins: NC does name situations where you must move insulation. Ask what would make you look underneath it.
q-ai-06.In each attic, at several spots, to chec: The SOP does not set a routine sampling quota. Think about what should trigger moving insulation instead.
q-ai-06.When the client asks and is present to w: The client's presence does not change your duty. Ask what you might see in the attic itself that should prompt you.

q-ai-07.Acceptable if the ladder holds your full: One successful climb proves little about brittle fasteners under shear. What happens on the hundredth trip with a heavy box?
q-ai-07.Cosmetic, since the ladder still folds a: Folding is not the concern here. Ask what holds the ladder to the framing while someone is standing on it.
q-ai-07.Not reportable, because attic stairs are: Ask whether any exclusion would really stop you from reporting a ladder that could detach under a person's weight.

q-ai-08.14 in by 20 in: Picture an adult with a flashlight squeezing through 14 by 20 in. Would that fit a body comfortably?
q-ai-08.18 in by 24 in: Close to some figures you may know, but the course number is larger on both sides. Picture an adult with tools fitting through.
q-ai-08.30 in by 36 in: That is near doorway size, not a ceiling hatch. Recall that one number in this rule belongs to the headroom above.

q-ai-09.Each one in the house: Operating every door and window is thorough, but ask whether the NC SOP actually demands all of them.
q-ai-09.Those in the bedrooms: Bedrooms matter for egress, but ask whether NC limits this duty to one type of room.
q-ai-09.One per floor of the house: A whole floor can hold many rooms with different problems. Ask what unit NC actually counts by.

q-ai-10.Repair item; recommend sanding and repai: Ask whether worn edge paint changes how the door works, and what kind of condition paint wear really is.
q-ai-10.Monitor for structural movement around t: Movement shows up as binding, sticking, or gaps. What did the stem say about how this door swings and latches?
q-ai-10.Refer to a carpenter to evaluate the doo: A referral needs a reason. Ask what defect a carpenter would actually be evaluating on this door.

q-ai-11.Nothing more; a fan that pulls air is wo: Pulling air at the grille shows the motor works. Ask what happens to that air after it leaves the room.
q-ai-11.The fan motor's amperage, using a clamp: Clamp meter readings on a fan motor go beyond a visual inspection. What could you check just by looking?
q-ai-11.The fan's noise rating, printed on the h: Noise is a comfort spec, not a defect. Think about what failure could make a working fan still a problem.

q-ai-12.Call it mold and recommend remediation b: Check what NC says about determining mold. Can you name a substance you cannot confirm by sight?
q-ai-12.Call it normal aging of the plywood shea: Plywood ages fairly evenly. Ask why darkening would cluster near the eaves if age alone caused it.
q-ai-12.Call it a roof leak and recommend roof r: Is one patch of discoloration enough to diagnose a leak, let alone justify a whole new roof?

q-dk-01.Acceptable if there are many nails at cl: More nails still means the same kind of fastener. Ask what kind of connection holds a ledger to the house framing.
q-dk-01.Acceptable on smaller decks, under about: Ask whether the fastener rule changes with deck size, or whether a small crowded deck still loads its ledger hard.
q-dk-01.Monitor it, unless the ledger is visibly: Waiting until the ledger visibly pulls away means waiting for the failure itself. How do nailed ledgers usually fail?

q-dk-02.To give the deck a finished look where i: Flashing hides under the siding laps. Ask what job a hidden part does, rather than how it looks.
q-dk-02.To keep termites and carpenter ants out: Termite shields exist, but this flashing sits at the top of the ledger. Think about what arrives there from above.
q-dk-02.To stop the ledger from swelling and exp: Wood movement from heat is small. Ask what slow, repeated exposure at the top of a ledger would cause.

q-dk-03.Brick is acceptable as long as the throu: Galvanizing protects a bolt from rust. Does it change what the bolt is anchored into?
q-dk-03.Bolts through brick hold better than lag: A bolt is only as good as what it grips. Ask how brick veneer is tied to the house behind it.
q-dk-03.It is a cosmetic concern, since the mort: Cracked mortar is the small worry. Ask what a deck full of people pulls on through those bolts.

q-dk-04.Acceptable if most of the holes are fill: A hanger's rated strength assumes a full fastener schedule. Ask what partial filling does to that rating.
q-dk-04.Acceptable, because screws are stronger: Stronger in what way? Think about how drywall screws behave under sideways shear, not just pull-out.
q-dk-04.Cosmetic, as long as the hangers are not: A straight hanger can still fail. Ask where the load actually transfers from the joist into the hanger.

q-dk-05.A 6 in sphere: That size belongs to a different spot on a stair guard. Ask what the general baluster rule is protecting.
q-dk-05.A 2 in sphere: That gap would be tighter than needed. Ask what body part the sphere stands for and roughly how big it is.
q-dk-05.A 5 in sphere: Think about the size of a small child's head, and which sphere sizes code commonly uses.

q-dk-06.On each deck, whatever its height above: A deck one step above the lawn does not need a guard. Ask what height actually triggers one.
q-dk-06.Above 48 in, measured at the deck's oute: Ask whether 48 in is the trigger you remember, and whether measuring only at the edge handles sloping ground.
q-dk-06.When the deck has stairs or is over 24 i: Stairs bring handrail rules, not guard rules. Check the height number you remember against the guard trigger.

q-dk-07.30 in: That number is the height that triggers a guard, not the guard's own height. Keep the two apart.
q-dk-07.32 in: Ask where 32 in comes from. Compare it with the guard trigger height and the residential guard figures you learned.
q-dk-07.48 in: Ask whether that figure fits a residential deck, or whether you are thinking of taller guards in other building types.

q-dk-08.To make the rail stiffer at the spot whe: Stiffness comes from posts and brackets along the run. Ask what risk lives at the open end itself.
q-dk-08.For appearance, so the rail looks neat a: Code cares little about looks. Think about what happens at the end of a rail as someone steps off the stairs.
q-dk-08.To keep rainwater from soaking into the: The return rule applies to metal rails too, which have no end grain. Think about the people using the rail.

q-dk-09.Acceptable, because ground-contact treat: Treated wood resists rot, but the stem says the base is already soft. What does a soft probe tell you?
q-dk-09.Monitor it, since the deck is not visibl: A post can lose strength before it leans. Ask what a soft base means for the load path right now.
q-dk-09.Not reportable, since probing is an inva: Check what NC says about probing where deterioration is suspected, for exterior wood and structural parts.

q-dk-10.10 psf: Think of a crowded party on the deck. Would 10 pounds per square foot cover that crowd?
q-dk-10.20 psf: Ask what the design case is for a deck. A packed party loads it more than you might expect.
q-dk-10.100 psf: Ask whether a residential deck is really designed like a warehouse floor, or around people and furniture.

q-rf-01.Walk on the roofing when it is safe to d: Check whether NC makes walking the roof a duty, even when it looks safe to do so.
q-rf-01.Inspect solar panels, antennas, and othe: Ask whether add-ons mounted on the roof fall under the roofing inspection, or are things the SOP sets aside.
q-rf-01.Certify the roof's remaining life for in: Inspectors describe and report conditions. Ask whether certifying a roof's remaining life fits that role.

q-rf-02.It is cosmetic until the rubber falls aw: Ask what the boot is there to stop, and whether a crack already lets that through.
q-rf-02.It restricts airflow through the plumbin: The boot wraps the outside of the pipe. Does a crack in it change anything inside the vent?
q-rf-02.Boots are part of plumbing, not the roof: Ask which system keeps water out at a roof penetration. Who would you send to fix the boot?

q-rf-03.1 in: One inch barely clears the roofing. Recall the general extension figure, not the smallest number you can picture.
q-rf-03.12 in: Ask whether you are mixing up the general rule with the higher figures used in snow country.
q-rf-03.3 ft: That rise belongs to special cases, such as a vent near an openable window. What is the general figure?

q-rf-04.Supplies combustion air to an attic furn: Ask whether a vent at the very top of the roof would make sense as a fresh air supply for a furnace.
q-rf-04.Cools the shingles from below to slow th: Ask what the ridge vent moves through the attic, rather than what it does to the shingles above it.
q-rf-04.Lets the roof deck expand along the ridg: Ask whether an opening at the ridge is about wood movement, or about the attic's air path.

q-rf-05.Shingle granule loss on the north-facing: Granules sit on the top surface of the shingles. Where would you stand to see that?
q-rf-05.Gutter condition and the downspout slope: Gutters hang outside at the eaves. Ask which items you could see only from inside the house.
q-rf-05.Chimney crown cracks and missing mortar: The crown caps the chimney outdoors. Where would you need to be to see it?

q-rf-06.Extend 1 ft above the landing, 1 ft out: Check both numbers. A ladder set that steep and barely above the edge is hard to step off safely.
q-rf-06.Rest against the gutter, 1 ft out per 4: Ask whether a gutter is built to carry a ladder plus a person's weight.
q-rf-06.Stand upright against the wall, 3 ft abo: Ask what keeps a ladder from tipping backward when it stands straight up against a wall.

q-rf-07.The roof covering, flashing, and the rid: Those parts keep water out of the roof. Ask which parts handle water once it has left the roof surface.
q-rf-07.Gutters, plus the municipal storm sewer: Ask where an inspector's scope ends. Is anything under the street part of the house you are inspecting?
q-rf-07.Interior floor drains and the sump pump: Ask whether these handle roof water, or water that is already inside or under the house.

q-rf-08.Antennae, satellite dishes, and their ro: Ask whether add-on accessories mounted on the roof are things the SOP requires or sets aside.
q-rf-08.Lightning arrestors and their ground wir: Think about which items are roofing components and which are accessories attached to the roof.
q-rf-08.De-icing cables along the eaves and gutt: Ask whether these are part of the roof itself, or an electrical accessory added to it.

q-ra-01.Bond the shingles together into one seal: Granules sit on the top surface, exposed to weather. Ask what they shield, rather than what they join.
q-ra-01.Seal around the nail holes when the sun: Nails are meant to be hidden under the next course. Would surface granules ever reach them?
q-ra-01.Make the shingle waterproof, so underlay: Ask whether a loose mineral coating could replace the underlayment layer. What is it shielding the asphalt from?

q-ra-02.They are cosmetic once the heads have ru: Rust is a sign of water at the nail. Ask where that water goes next.
q-ra-02.They matter in hurricane zones, not in n: Ask whether the problem needs extreme wind, or whether ordinary rain on an exposed nail head is enough.
q-ra-02.Exposed nails are normal along the ridge: Ask what covers the nails at ridge and hip caps on a correct install. Should heads be showing anywhere?

q-ra-03.Through the exposed tab, so the wind wil: Ask what happens each time rain hits a nail head left out in the open.
q-ra-03.Above the nailing line, near the top edg: Nails set too high can miss the shingle below. Ask what that does to wind resistance.
q-ra-03.On the exposed tab, as long as each head: Sealant on an exposed head ages in the sun. Ask whether a properly placed nail ever needs that sealant.

q-ra-04.Supports the gutter and keeps it pitched: Ask whether a thin metal strip at the roof edge is built to carry a gutter full of water.
q-ra-04.Decorative trim that hides the cut edge: Ask what would happen at the roof edge without it, beyond how the edge looks.
q-ra-04.Vents the attic at the eave, like a soff: Drip edge is solid metal at the edge of the deck. Ask whether air passes through it at all.

q-ra-05.Shingles from both planes are woven toge: Weaving is its own valley method. Ask what the word cut in closed-cut suggests.
q-ra-05.An open metal channel is left exposed, w: Ask what the word closed suggests about whether any valley metal shows.
q-ra-05.Shingles from each side meet at the cent: Valleys collect water from two roof planes. Would any accepted method skip underlayment there?

q-ra-06.1:12, with double underlayment below 3:1: Asphalt shingles shed water by lapping. Ask whether a slope that flat lets them shed water at all.
q-ra-06.3:12, with double underlayment above 6:1: Ask whether steeper slopes need more protection or less. Water moves faster as the roof gets steeper.
q-ra-06.4:12, with double underlayment from 4:12: Ask where extra underlayment belongs: at the steeper end, or at the low-slope end where water slows down.

q-ra-07.6 in past the outer edge of the gutter: The ice barrier is laid on the roof deck, not on the gutter. Where does an ice dam push water?
q-ra-07.12 in up the roof from the drip edge: Ice dams back water up the slope. Ask whether a foot of barrier reaches far enough past where it pools.
q-ra-07.36 in up the slope from the eave edge: Ask which reference point the rule uses. Distances measured from the eave edge change with every overhang width.

q-ra-08.A third layer is fine if longer nails re: Longer nails fix how far a nail reaches. Do they fix the added weight, or the deck you can no longer see?
q-ra-08.Re-covering is better, since the old lay: Ask whether shingles are installed for insulation at all, and what the old layers hide underneath.
q-ra-08.Layer count does not matter for asphalt: Ask what each extra layer adds to the roof framing, and what it hides from the roofer.

q-fd-01.Normal shrinkage of the mortar as it slo: Ask whether curing shrinkage would follow a long, stepped diagonal path through many joints.
q-fd-01.Lateral soil pressure pushing the wall i: Ask which crack pattern goes with a wall pushed inward. Is it stepped and diagonal, or does it run along one course?
q-fd-01.Freeze-thaw damage to the block faces an: Freeze-thaw tends to damage the faces of the blocks. Ask what a crack stepping through the joints points to.

q-fd-02.It is typical shrinkage of block walls a: Shrinkage does not push a wall out of plane. Ask what the inward bow tells you.
q-fd-02.It comes from the house settling evenly: Even settling moves the whole house down together. Would that bow one wall inward?
q-fd-02.It is cosmetic once it has been painted: Paint can hide a crack, but can it stop a wall that is still moving?

q-fd-03.Mold growth on the block; recommend prof: Ask whether this deposit is living growth, and remember NC excludes determining mold.
q-fd-03.Early structural failure of the block fa: The stem says the wall is otherwise sound. Ask whether a surface deposit alone shows structural damage.
q-fd-03.Termite mud tubes; refer to a pest contr: Mud tubes are brown, earthy tunnels. Ask whether white powder on a wall face matches that.

q-fd-04.Acceptable, since masonry piers crack as: Ask whether a crack running through several blocks is the same as minor aging in the mortar.
q-fd-04.Patch it with mortar and note it as repa: Patching is repair work and hides the evidence. Ask what an inspector does instead of fixing.
q-fd-04.Monitor it, since the pier is not leanin: A pier can lose capacity before it leans. Ask what this pier carries and how much rests on it.

q-fd-05.Acceptable; stacked shims are a normal w: Shims can be used, but ask whether loose and crushed shims still give the girder solid support.
q-fd-05.Cosmetic, as long as the floor above fee: A floor can feel level today and settle later. Ask what crushed shims mean for the support under the girder.
q-fd-05.Not reportable without first calculating: NC excludes calculating loads. Does that stop you from reporting what you can plainly see?

q-fd-06.10 ft apart, with one within 36 in of ea: Ask whether bolts that far apart would keep a house from sliding under lateral load. Recall both numbers.
q-fd-06.4 ft apart, with two bolts at each plate: Ask whether the rule you remember calls for paired bolts at the ends, or a single bolt near each end.
q-fd-06.8 ft apart, with one at the center of ea: Ask where a plate is most likely to lift or slide: at its middle, or near its ends?

q-fd-07.The depth and width of the footings belo: Footings below grade are not visible. Ask what you can describe without digging.
q-fd-07.The compressive strength of the foundati: Ask whether NC asks you to measure strength, or to describe something you can see.
q-fd-07.The soil type and its bearing capacity b: Ask whether soil bearing capacity is something an inspector can judge by eye, or an engineer's job.

q-fd-08.Calculate the load on the pier to judge: Check what NC says about calculating strength or adequacy. Who does that work?
q-fd-08.Specify the repair method so the seller: Ask whether reporting methods of correction is part of your role, or someone else's.
q-fd-08.Estimate the cost of a new pier for nego: Ask whether NC lets inspectors report costs of correction, even when the client wants a number.

q-rt-01.Walk on the tiles near the center of eac: Ask what happens to clay tile under a person's weight, wherever on the slope you step.
q-rt-01.Walk on the tiles along the ridge, where: Ask whether any part of a clay tile roof is safe to walk, and who pays if a tile breaks.
q-rt-01.Lift a few tiles to see the condition of: Lifting tile is a disruptive step that can break it. Ask what NC expects of a visual roof inspection.

q-rt-02.It is cosmetic, since tile is mostly the: Ask what job the tile does for the layer beneath it, beyond appearance.
q-rt-02.Cracked tile still sheds water; replace: A cracked tile may shed some water. Ask what it no longer shields underneath.
q-rt-02.It matters on new roofs still under warr: Ask whether the damage a crack allows depends on the roof's age or its warranty status.

q-rt-03.Normal thermal movement of the tiles in: Ask whether ordinary heat movement would pull tiles fully out of their courses.
q-rt-03.The roof slope is too steep to hold the: Tile roofs are commonly installed on steep slopes. Ask what normally holds each tile in place.
q-rt-03.An installation laid too tight, pushing: Ask which direction a too-tight fit would push tiles, and whether that matches tiles sliding down at the eave.

q-rt-04.The tiles themselves, which are fully wa: Ask what reaches the deck through laps, cracks, and gaps between tiles in wind-driven rain.
q-rt-04.The mortar packed between the tiles at t: Ask whether mortar at the laps forms a continuous sheet across the whole roof deck.
q-rt-04.The glaze or sealer coating on the tile: A glaze sits on the tile face. Ask whether it covers the gaps between tiles.

q-rt-05.2:12; double underlayment up to 4:12: That figure belongs to a different roof covering in this course. Ask whether tile shares it.
q-rt-05.1-1/2:12; double underlayment up to 3:12: Ask whether tile, which sheds by lapping, could handle a slope flatter than the asphalt shingle minimum.
q-rt-05.3-1/2:12; double underlayment up to 6:12: Check both numbers against the asphalt rule you know. Is tile's minimum really that far above it?

q-rt-06.Major defect; mortar fails over time: Ask whether a future possibility is the same as a defect you can see today.
q-rt-06.Repair item; recommend repointing: Repointing fixes mortar that is cracked or loose. What did the stem say about this mortar?
q-rt-06.Monitor it and re-inspect yearly: Ask what observed condition would justify a monitoring note on mortar described as intact.

q-rt-07.It is in scope and inspected the same as: Check what NC .1107 says about buildings that stand apart from the house.
q-rt-07.It may not be inspected, even if the cli: Ask whether an exclusion forbids extra work, or just means it is not required by default.
q-rt-07.Its electrical and roof are inspected, n: Ask whether the SOP carves out particular systems of a detached building, or treats the building as a whole.

q-rt-08.A roof that holds shingles will hold til: Ask whether shingles and tile weigh about the same per square foot of roof.
q-rt-08.The underlayment needs upgrading, but no: Ask what carries the weight of the roof covering, and whether it was sized for something heavier.
q-rt-08.Tile is lighter than asphalt, so framing: Picture lifting a single clay tile and a single shingle. Which one weighs more?

q-eg-01.36 in above the floor: Lower sills are allowed; the question asks for the highest permitted. Is that figure really this low?
q-eg-01.48 in above the floor: Picture a small child or an impaired adult trying to climb over a sill four feet up.
q-eg-01.54 in above the floor: Picture a small child trying to climb over a sill at an adult's chest height. Could they?

q-eg-02.Bedrooms on upper floors, not the ground: Ask whether a sleeping person on the ground floor is any less likely to be trapped by a fire.
q-eg-02.Each habitable room, including the kitch: Ask who is most likely to be trapped in a fire, and which rooms they would be in.
q-eg-02.The primary bedroom and the basement: Ask whether a child asleep in a secondary bedroom faces less risk in a fire than the owners.

q-eg-03.4 sq ft, with 24 in of projection and wi: Picture an adult climbing into a 2 ft by 2 ft well. Would that leave room to climb back out?
q-eg-03.10 sq ft, with 42 in of projection and w: Recheck both numbers, and ask whether the projection and width you picked actually produce the area listed.
q-eg-03.7 sq ft, with 32 in of projection and wi: Picture an adult in a winter coat climbing out of a well under 3 ft across. Is there room?

q-eg-04.Acceptable, since the bars improve the b: Ask what those bars do to the window's job as an escape route in a fire.
q-eg-04.Cosmetic, as long as the bars are painte: Ask whether paint condition matters when someone needs out through this window at night.
q-eg-04.Acceptable if the bedroom door leads to: Ask whether a hallway full of smoke still counts as a way out from that bedroom.

q-eg-05.Mark them acceptable, since a release le: A lever you have not tried tells you it exists, not that it works. What should the client learn?
q-eg-05.Operate the release yourself, using forc: Not required to operate does not mean you should force it. Ask what forcing a mechanism could break.
q-eg-05.Report them as a code violation and reco: Inspectors are not code officials. Ask whether a release lever makes removal the right recommendation.

q-eg-06.A 4 in sphere must not pass: The 4 in rule covers most of the guard. Ask whether the stair triangle is treated the same way.
q-eg-06.A 2 in sphere must not pass: That gap would be tighter than anywhere else on the guard. Ask whether the triangle is stricter or looser.
q-eg-06.No test applies to the triangle: Ask whether a child could slip through that triangle if no rule applied to it.

q-eg-07.A door from the garage into an inside ha: A hallway is a common garage connection. Ask what would make one connection more hazardous than another.
q-eg-07.A solid 1-3/8 in door from the garage in: Notice the door spec given. Ask why a course would name a solid door of that thickness.
q-eg-07.An overhead door with photo-eyes and an: Photo-eyes and auto-reverse are safety features. Ask whether they sound like what the course calls hazardous.

q-eg-08.28 in of clear width and 72 in of height: Six feet of height would make many adults duck. Recall the IRC minimums, which are larger on both counts.
q-eg-08.36 in of clear width and 84 in of height: Ask whether you are remembering a common door size rather than the minimum clear opening the IRC requires.
q-eg-08.30 in of clear width and 80 in of height: 80 in is a common door height. Ask whether you are remembering the door slab, not the IRC clear opening figures.

q-eg-09.18 in: Ask whether a step this low would really need a guard. Recall the height that triggers one.
q-eg-09.24 in: Ask whether you are remembering a figure from another rule. Recheck the guard trigger height.
q-eg-09.42 in: That is closer to guard heights in other building types. Ask what height above the floor triggers a residential guard.

q-pl-01.It drains too slowly and clogs more than: Ask what the trap's water seal is for, and how the S shape treats that seal as water rushes through.
q-pl-01.It is a dated style choice with no real: Model code prohibits S-traps. Ask what a mere style difference would fail to explain about that ban.
q-pl-01.It wastes water each time the fixture is: Ask what happens to the water left in the trap after the fixture drains, rather than how much water flows.

q-pl-02.1/2 to 1 in: Ask how long a shallow seal would last against evaporation or a siphoning pull.
q-pl-02.4 to 6 in: Ask what a deep seal collects over time at the bottom of the trap.
q-pl-02.6 to 8 in: A very deep seal holds standing water low in the trap. Ask what settles there over time.

q-pl-03.Yes, cycle each stop to prove it shuts o: Ask what can happen when an old stop valve that has not moved in years gets turned.
q-pl-03.Yes, but just the hot side, where scale: Ask whether the hot side is any safer to turn, and what NC actually requires for valves.
q-pl-03.Yes, if the client asks you to check the: Ask whether the client's request changes the leak risk of turning an old stop.

q-pl-04.It is the modern standard, replacing rig: Ask whether flexible corrugated pipe is listed as an approved trap or drain material.
q-pl-04.It is acceptable if the run is short and: Ask whether a short run changes what the inside ridges do to grease and food waste.
q-pl-04.It matters at bathroom sinks, not at the: Ask which sink sends more grease and food waste down the drain. Does that help the case?

q-pl-05.Acceptable, since drain joints drip now: Ask whether any active leak at a drain joint is normal, and what it does to the wood below.
q-pl-05.Not reportable, because the crawlspace i: Ask whether NC excludes a crawlspace you can see into, or what you observe there.
q-pl-05.Monitor it and re-check at the final wal: Ask what a hidden crawlspace leak does to the framing in the weeks before anyone looks again.

q-pl-06.Report it as polybutylene, a known failu: Read the print on the pipe. Ask how polybutylene usually looks and whether this matches.
q-pl-06.Report it as a defect, since plastic sup: Ask whether modern approved supply materials include any plastics.
q-pl-06.Recommend replacing it with galvanized s: Ask why you would recommend replacing piping that is labeled, supported, and protected.

q-pl-07.6 to 12 in: Ask what a short standpipe does when a washer pumps out water fast.
q-pl-07.12 to 18 in: Ask whether this range is tall enough to catch the surge from a washer's pump without spilling.
q-pl-07.42 to 60 in: Ask what a very tall standpipe does to the trap below as fast water falls through it.

q-pl-08.Acceptable, since toilets can rock a lit: Ask what sits under the toilet base that movement could disturb.
q-pl-08.Cosmetic, once the caulk at the base is: Caulk hides a gap but does not anchor anything. Ask what the rocking does underneath.
q-pl-08.Tighten the flange bolts yourself and mo: Ask whether repairs are an inspector's job, and what tightening could crack or hide.

q-pl-09.A flow rate of at least 5 gallons per mi: Ask whether NC defines this term by a measured number, or by how fixtures work in use.
q-pl-09.Steady flow at the kitchen faucet with n: Ask whether one fixture running alone tests the system the way a busy household uses it.
q-pl-09.Static water pressure above 40 psi at th: Static pressure is read with nothing flowing. Ask whether that tells you how fixtures perform in use.

q-pl-10.40 psi: Ask whether that figure is the high or the low end of a comfortable pressure range.
q-pl-10.60 psi: Ask whether 60 psi would stress hoses and valves, or sits comfortably within the typical range.
q-pl-10.120 psi: Ask how long hoses and the water heater would sit under stress before pressure climbed that high.

q-pl-11.Whether the water supply is public or a: Check whether NC asks you to decide the source of the supply, or to describe something you can see on site.
q-pl-11.The water quality from the well, by test: Ask whether testing water quality fits a visual inspection under NC rules.
q-pl-11.Whether a backflow device is present at: Check what NC says about backflow devices before listing one as a required description.

q-pl-12.To let rainwater in to flush the drain l: Ask whether anyone would want rainwater entering a drain system through the roof.
q-pl-12.To cool the drain pipes when hot water i: Ask whether drain pipes need cooling at all, and what else a vent might carry.
q-pl-12.To raise water pressure at the upper fix: Drains and supply are separate systems. Ask whether a drain vent could affect supply pressure.

q-st-01.Acceptable if the cut is small and near: Ask whether a truss member has spare capacity to give up, even near its ends.
q-st-01.Acceptable if the ceiling below has no c: Ask whether a ceiling that looks fine today proves the truss is carrying its load as designed.
q-st-01.Repair it by nailing a scrap board over: Ask who designs a truss repair, and whether an inspector should be fixing anything.

q-st-02.One-half of the joist depth (D/2): Picture a joist with half its depth cut away. Would the outer thirds still carry their load?
q-st-02.One-third of the joist depth (D/3): Ask whether you are remembering the hole rule rather than the notch rule. They use different fractions.
q-st-02.One-quarter of the joist depth (D/4): D/4 is a real notch figure. Ask which location along the span it applies to.

q-st-03.No larger than D/2, close to the top or: Ask where in a joist the fibers carry the most stress, and whether a hole belongs there.
q-st-03.No larger than D/6, at least 2 in from e: D/6 belongs to a different rule. Ask whether holes and notches share the same limit.
q-st-03.As large as needed, as long as it is cen: Centering helps, but ask whether a hole of any size leaves enough wood to carry the load.

q-st-04.Structural movement; refer to an enginee: Ask what signs of movement you would expect: offset, widening, binding doors. Does the stem show any?
q-st-04.Foundation failure; recommend underpinni: Ask whether a single hairline crack justifies a major repair, and whether recommending methods is your role.
q-st-04.Moisture damage; refer to a roofer to fi: Ask what evidence of water the stem gives you. A taped joint crack alone shows no staining.

q-st-05.Dead load is snow on the roof; live load: Model code treats snow and wind as their own load types. Ask what dead and live each describe.
q-st-05.Dead load is what a failed member carrie: Ask whether these terms describe a member's condition, or the kinds of weight a building carries.
q-st-05.They are two names for the same total de: If the two terms meant the same thing, why would NC define a structural component as carrying both?

q-st-06.Joists to trusses to walls to footings t: Trusses carry the roof. Ask what floor joists rest on in a crawlspace house built on piers.
q-st-06.Girder to joists to piers to footings to: Ask which member is larger and collects load from the others. Which one bears on which?
q-st-06.Joists to piers to girder to footings to: Ask whether a pier sits under the girder or above it. Trace which member rests on which.

q-st-07.Foundation settlement under the interior: Ask whether settlement would open a gap in winter and close it again every summer.
q-st-07.Seasonal shrinkage of the drywall tape a: Ask whether tape shrinkage would reverse itself each summer. What could move back and forth with the seasons?
q-st-07.Roof leaks soaking and sagging the ceili: A wet, sagging ceiling would show stains, and it would not close up on its own each summer.

q-st-08.The adequacy of the foundation anchor bo: Judging whether bolting is adequate takes calculation. Ask whether a visual SOP expects that from you.
q-st-08.The load capacity of each floor joist an: Could you know a joist's load capacity just by looking at it with a flashlight?
q-st-08.The engineering design of the roof truss: Ask whether reviewing a truss system's engineering design is something an inspector does on site.
